_comment: The LOCKED Basketwatch fleet. This file is the decision, not a suggestion: score.py renders registry.md from it and fails loudly if a locked site is no longer fleet-ready. Change the fleet by editing this file, never by re-running a picker.
rationale: Eight real stores, four per country, spanning five extraction shapes (json-ld, graphql, bare-html, spa-with-state, spa-opaque) so a breakage in one does not resemble a breakage in another. Weighted toward genuine grocers over online pantries per docs/prd.md section 2.6, and toward sites already proven end to end. Clears the PRD bar of 4+ US scrapers plus the clone store, with PH included. Members split into two roles. Index contributors supply the basket on both sides. The US source is ethnic grocers, which stock generic staples and fresh produce where the supermarket chains publish nothing and the online pantries sell diet goods. Reliability subjects scrape cleanly across different markup shapes and carry the self-healing story without feeding the index.

fleet.name: Shop Gaisano
fleet.why_locked: Top-scoring site in the whole registry. Server-rendered json-ld, 10/10 basket categories off a 1,406-URL sitemap, Visayas/Mindanao regional chain with no prebuilt scraper anywhere. Proven end to end on rice 5kg, the PH basket anchor item.

fleet.name: Ever Supermarket
fleet.why_locked: Best basket coverage of any store in the registry: 10/10 core items, 19/20 tracked, every one with a computed unit price, and genuine staples throughout - Farmboy Pandan Rice 5kg, whole chicken 1kg, a 30-egg tray. Shopify search makes selection reliable.
fleet.caveat: Was scored 85/backup on sitemap-derived basket coverage of 0/10. Its catalogue was only visible through Shopify search - a reminder that sitemap coverage understates any store with a search API.

fleet.name: Shop Suki
fleet.why_locked: 16 of 20 items settled with strong picks - Nestle Fresh Milk 1L, Angelina Super Loaf 640g, Balducci Spaghetti 500g, real white onions sold by weight, Absolute Distilled Water 6L. Server-rendered json-ld and a broad staples catalogue.
fleet.caveat: Its chicken pick is Marca Manok Sinandomeng Rice - 'manok' is the brand, not the contents - and its eggs pick is salted egg. Both need curating in manual-basket.json before use.

fleet.name: SM Markets
fleet.why_locked: Largest PH supermarket network and the broadest PH catalogue. Pages are a client-rendered shell, but the public Magento GraphQL endpoint is a structured fallback no selector change can break. Proven end to end.

fleet.name: MerryMart Wholesale
fleet.why_locked: Fully server-rendered PHP prices with no structured data at all - the bare-HTML shape the fleet otherwise lacks on the PH side, and the one most likely to break on a redesign, which makes it a good heal subject.
fleet.caveat: Wholesale case pricing. Needs per-unit normalisation before its numbers enter the basket index.

catalogue.note: no sitemap; product URLs come from the homepage-to-category crawl in vet.py

fleet.name: Landers Superstore
fleet.why_locked: 10/10 basket categories from a 17,032-URL sitemap - the deepest basket coverage of any PH site - and a well-known consumer name for the demo.
fleet.caveat: Highest-risk member. Prices render client-side and the backing APIs (api.landers.ph, Unbxd search) are private, so there is no non-browser fallback. If its Studio scraper proves flaky, swap in Southstar Drug, which is server-rendered microdata.

catalogue.coverage_reason: 17,032 products and client-rendered pages; a full pull would dominate the budget
catalogue.note: Confirmed client-rendered: 0 rows from 300 pages with current code, and no price in raw HTML even through the Unlocker. Needs the Studio transport, which drives a real browser. Its 20 pinned basket items still work today.

studio.note: Two heals. Yields roughly 1 usable row per 10 URLs on /food-cupboard/, 4 of 5 on /anti-hoarding-and-anti-panic-buying-list/. Still strictly better than the 0 rows HTTP produces, and the only access path this store has.

fleet.name: Kesar Grocery
fleet.why_locked: The US index source. 13 of 20 items settled, 7/10 core, every one unit-priced, and genuinely generic goods including fresh produce: Basmati 4LB, whole wheat bread 24oz, Great Value elbow pasta 1LB, Amul cheese 1KG, organic bananas 3lb, beefsteak tomatoes, white onions, gala apples, navel oranges. 11,987 products in its sitemap and no structured data at all, which is why it needed bare-HTML extraction to surface.
fleet.caveat: Its cooking-oil pick is almond oil rather than a neutral cooking oil; curate before use. Bare-HTML extraction means no structured data to fall back on, so a redesign hits harder here than on a json-ld site - which also makes it a good heal subject.

catalogue.coverage_reason: 11,987 products; a bounded slice keeps the cost sane

fleet.name: MexGrocer
fleet.why_locked: Second US index source and a different cuisine, so the two do not share supply. 9 items settled, 5/10 core, Shopify search for reliable selection. Mahatma Long Grain Rice and Cafe de Olla ground coffee are real staples.
fleet.caveat: Blocked on plain HTTP for page fetches but its Shopify search API answers fine. Chicken resolves to bouillon and bananas to banana leaves; both need curating.

catalogue.note: blocked on plain HTTP; its Shopify endpoints answer through the Unlocker

fleet.name: Dierbergs
fleet.why_locked: Authentic St. Louis regional grocer with clean json-ld and real basket staples. Proven end to end on a bread SKU.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

fleet.name: The Fresh Market
fleet.why_locked: Specialty national grocer, 9/10 basket categories, server-rendered json-ld reachable without the Unlocker. Highest-scoring authentic US grocer after Dierbergs.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

catalogue.note: Sitemap holds 50 URLs and none are products - gift cards and recall notices. Re-verified with current code: 20 rows, 0 with a price. Not a rendering problem; there is no public product catalogue to pull.

fleet.name: Wegmans
fleet.why_locked: Major regional grocer that ships prices inside embedded page state rather than markup - a distinct extraction shape from the json-ld sites, and a realistic breakage mode.
fleet.caveat: Only 4/10 basket categories surfaced from its sitemap; confirm SKU coverage before relying on it for the index.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

catalogue.note: Sitemap holds 175 URLs, all /shop/discovery/ and /shop/featured/ landing pages rather than products. Re-verified with current code: 0 rows from 175 pages. No public product catalogue to pull.

fleet.name: Meijer
fleet.why_locked: Midwest supercenter, 8/10 basket categories, plain HTML pricing with no structured data - the bare-HTML shape on the US side. Promoted from the bench after Grocery Outlet failed the lock audit.
fleet.caveat: Needs the Web Unlocker on every run, so it is the only locked site with a per-run credit cost. Budget for it in the scheduler.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

catalogue.note: no public catalogue at all - excluded from the pull

fleet.name: Cypress Indian Grocery
fleet.why_locked: The most realistic US prices found anywhere in the registry: Royal Basmati 10lb at $3.75/kg, Domino Brown Sugar 2lb at $4.62/kg, Aara Sunflower Oil 5L at $3.40/L. Ordinary supermarket-level pricing on generic staples, not specialty markups.

fleet.name: Latimex Market
fleet.why_locked: Latin American grocer, 9 items settled with clean unit prices and a different cuisine from MexGrocer, so the two do not share supply.
fleet.caveat: Skews premium - Bomba rice at $19.99/kg and extra virgin olive oil rather than a neutral cooking oil. Good for breadth, not for the cheapest-basket claim.

fleet.name: MexMax
fleet.why_locked: Measured 8/10 core basket items through its Shopify search API - the single best US store found so far, and the one that fixes the US gaps that mattered: eggs, chicken and cooking oil each appeared in exactly one US store before this. Mexican grocery wholesaler, 2,643-URL sitemap, products.json paginates at 250.

fleet.name: Amigo Foods
fleet.why_locked: Measured 6/10 core items: rice, bread, pasta, coffee, sugar, bananas. US Latin grocer with a 2,741-URL sitemap and a working products.json. Adds a second US source for five of the ten core items.

fleet.name: Lili Mart
fleet.why_locked: Measured 6/10 core items and the only new US store carrying milk. US Filipino grocer selling the same brands as the PH fleet, which makes a like-for-like US/PH comparison possible on identical goods rather than on a currency conversion between different products.

fleet.name: Sukli
fleet.why_locked: Measured 3/10 core items - bread, coffee, rice - which clears the bar without clearing it comfortably. Locked for the same reason as Lili Mart: a US Filipino grocer stocking PH brands is the cleanest available US-versus-PH price comparison. Thin, and marked as such.
fleet.caveat: 3/10 core items measured. Included for cross-country comparability, not depth.

fleet.name: H Mart
fleet.why_locked: Korean-American chain with real US retail presence and a 1,520-URL sitemap. No products.json - /products.json returns 404 - so it takes the sitemap method rather than the Shopify one. Registry scored its basket coverage at 8/10 from sitemap keywords, which is the weaker measure; treat that as unverified until a pull confirms it.
fleet.caveat: Basket coverage is sitemap-derived, not measured. No bulk endpoint.

catalogue.coverage_reason: 1,520 products and one fetch per page; capped at 300

always_in_fleet.name: Parker's Pantry
always_in_fleet.why_locked: The clone store on the VPS subdomain. Disclosed test rig with a layout-mutation switch; it is the scripted break-detect-heal demo centerpiece per docs/prd.md section 2.5, not a real retailer, so it is not scored in the registry.

bench._comment: Named substitutes, already vetted, promote without re-running discovery.

changelog.why: A clean no-cache re-probe with TLS verification and a tightened price regex reclassified Grocery Outlet from server_rendered to spa_empty. Its original verdict rested on a homepage banner asset (012126_eggs_websitebanner_) that the product-URL scorer mistook for a product page; vet.py now rejects marketing-asset slugs. Meijer was the named bench substitute for the bare-HTML slot.

changelog.change: Split the fleet into index contributors and reliability subjects
changelog.why: Building the per-store basket showed the four US members settle 0-4 of the core 10 items - not a scraping failure but a catalogue one. Round 4 hunted specifically for US retailers publishing staples and found none across co-ops, Hispanic and Asian grocers, delivery-first grocers and US Filipino grocers. Sukli and Lili Mart both looked ideal on structure and both turned out to sell snacks and specialty goods. Rather than drop working scrapers or pretend they feed the index, each member now declares which job it does.

changelog.change: Added Ever Supermarket as an index contributor
changelog.why: Testing every store with a search API through its own search rather than its sitemap surfaced Ever at 10/10 core items - better than any locked member. The registry had it at backup because sitemap keyword coverage read 0/10, which is the wrong measure for a store whose catalogue is only reachable by query.

changelog.change: Added Shop Suki as an index contributor
changelog.why: Found by searching for PH grocers on queryable platforms after Ever showed that sitemap-derived coverage understates stores whose catalogue is query-only. The PH index now rests on six contributors rather than four.

changelog.change: Added Kesar Grocery and MexGrocer as US index contributors
changelog.why: The earlier conclusion that no US retailer publishes plain staples was drawn from the wrong segment. Rounds 1-4 tested supermarket chains, diet pantries and snack importers; US ethnic grocers were never tested through their own search or with bare-HTML extraction. Kesar Grocery sells generic staples and fresh produce with 11,987 products in its sitemap, and publishes no structured data at all - which is exactly why it stayed invisible. The US side now contributes to the index.

changelog.change: Added Cypress Indian Grocery and Latimex Market
changelog.why: Round 6 basket-tested the round-5 candidates that had Shopify APIs but had only ever been judged on their sitemaps - the same measurement error that hid Ever Supermarket. Cypress Indian returned the most realistic US prices in the registry. US index contributors go from 2 to 4.

changelog.change: Corrected the catalogue status of The Fresh Market and Wegmans
changelog.why: Both were labelled needs_browser on the assumption that a zero-row pull meant client-rendering. Re-running them with current code disproved that: their sitemaps carry no product URLs at all - gift cards and recall notices for The Fresh Market, landing pages for Wegmans. They are now method:none, the same as Meijer. The original zero-row results were also produced by a long-running process holding pre-fix code in memory, which is why they needed re-checking rather than trusting.

changelog.change: Locked five US stores; rejected Kalustyan's; recorded that registry basket_coverage is not a measurement
changelog.why: The US fleet was too thin to be credible - eggs, milk, chicken and pasta each appeared in exactly one US store, so those series were one breakage from a hole. Eighteen US sites were already vetted fleet_ready and unused, so no discovery was needed. Measuring five of them through their Shopify search APIs contradicted the registry: its basket_coverage counts keyword hits in a sitemap, and all five read 10/10 there. Measured, they are MexMax 8/10, Amigo Foods 6/10, Lili Mart 6/10, Sukli 3/10 and Kalustyan's 0/10 - its 'rice' hit was a rice cooker. Four locked, Kalustyan's rejected despite a registry score of 100. H Mart joins on the sitemap method after /products.json returned 404. Cost: nothing, all free HTTP.

changelog.change: Added per-store studio blocks: template, seed URL, submission cap and cost class
changelog.why: Studio becomes the primary collector, so each store needs a collector built against a representative page. Sitemap-method stores get the product-page template and a real product URL; bulk-endpoint stores get the listing-page template and a paginated collection URL, because pointing an AI page-scraper at a raw products.json endpoint asks it to parse a bulk JSON API - fragile, and strictly worse than the free HTTP requests that already work. Every seed URL was checked live for a 200 before being written here. Status starts at 'pending' for all 16; nothing runs through Studio until a verification run promotes it.

changelog.change: Studio pilot on ph-landers: created, born broken, healed, now producing unit prices
changelog.why: Landers was the right pilot precisely because it is the only fleet store with no alternative: 0 rows from 300 HTTP pages, no price even through the Unlocker. The generated collector shipped broken - hostname as product name, no price, no error raised - and one `scraper heal --auto-approve --auto-save` fixed it. 4 of 5 URLs now return real prices and unit prices. Whole pilot cost $0.02, which settles the open cost question: Studio for the fleet is affordable. The run also exposed a data bug worth keeping: the collector returned size '1G' for a product titled '1Gal.', which parses as one gram and priced the oil at PHP 799,950/kg. Conflicting sizes now yield no unit price at all.

catalogue_policy.max_pages_semantics: API methods count pages of ~250 products; sitemap methods count individual product pages. Both are hard stops, checked before each fetch.
catalogue_policy.why_bounded: An unbounded Studio description once crawled ~150 pages and 4,470 rows (docs/hackathon-brief.md). Declaring the ceiling here makes a runaway impossible by construction and keeps the bound visible in the file that records fleet decisions.
catalogue_policy.tuning: These are starting values chosen to prove the pipeline, not final. Raise max_pages per store once per-run cost is measured.
catalogue_policy.history: A price row is written only when a product's price changes. Every run also writes a summary row (rows, pages, coverage) so checkRowCount can tell a truncated pull from a real price move.
catalogue_policy.studio_transport: Studio is the primary collector; catalogue.py is the fallback. A store enters a Studio run only once its studio.status reads 'ready', which requires a recorded verification run - an unproven collector can never enter the fleet by default. max_urls bounds what is submitted; the creation description separately bounds what the collector does with each URL it is given. Both are needed: max_pages could not have prevented the 4,470-row incident, because that was one page crawling onward.
